title: Act 3: The Frame
trigger: shared custody won, custody permanently denied, or deployment death

quests.name: The Frame
quests.summary: The adult child stops controlling the reconstructed parent and enters the record as themself.

stages.objective: Let the city lose color and the interface pull beyond the screen edge.
Listen to Sam explain which jobs were memories he supplied.
As the adult child, decide how much testimony can become belief.
Hear ten recorded choices re-voiced by the child.
Close the reconstruction with Forgiveness, Honor, The Cycle, or The File Closed.

nodes.stage: Sound stops in the middle of a room tone. Halvern's sodium orange drains to gray. The camera rises past the courthouse ceiling, past the map border, past a thin black bezel nobody had been shown.
nodes.text: The city occupies a laptop screen on a kitchen table.

choices.text: Pull back.

nodes.stage: Beside the laptop: twenty-four labeled tapes, returned envelopes, court copies, a service ribbon, an evidence photograph of a bracelet. Older hands rest near the keyboard. They belong to {{childName}}, now grown.
nodes.text: The creased photograph lies face down between the hands.

choices.text: Turn it over.
Look across the table.

nodes.stage: Sam Okafor sits across the table. His beard is white. His voice is the same voice from the pawn shop, without the compression of memory.
nodes.text: SAM: That is as far as the records take us cleanly.

choices.text: You gave them the lamp job.
You knew this whole time.

nodes.speaker: Sam Okafor
nodes.text: I told you about a lamp. Your program made it a job because jobs have edges. Life was less considerate.

choices.text: Did it happen?

nodes.speaker: Sam Okafor
nodes.text: Knew what? That you were asking your way into a person? Yes. That I could give you the person? No.

choices.text: Did any of it happen the way I played it?

nodes.speaker: Sam Okafor
nodes.text: The pawn ticket happened. Your parent's hands happened. The choice is where memory starts charging interest.
On the street line, I knew them through this counter. On the Army line, I knew them through the veterans hall. You made both versions use my face because the box needed one witness it could trust.

choices.text: Could I trust you?
Why did you let me make you younger?

nodes.text: For dates? Mostly. For prices? Check my ledger. For what your parent meant? I was a friend, not a warrant.

choices.text: You kept the ribbon.

nodes.text: You did not ask permission. It was flattering for ten minutes.

choices.text: You kept the ribbon.

nodes.text: I kept an envelope. You put the ribbon in it because empty evidence bothered you.

choices.text: What bothered you?

nodes.text: How badly you wanted the story to rule one way. Good parent. Bad parent. Hero. File. People become easy right before we stop seeing them.
I kept trying to arrive at a verdict because court records taught me that every room ends with one.

choices.text: Believe the choices that cost them something.
Believe only what two records agree on.
Stop asking belief to do memory's job.

nodes.text: Cost can prove commitment. It can also prove there was nothing cheaper left. Still, I understand why I kept those scenes.

choices.text: Keep the heirloom choice as played.
Mark every uncertain scene as uncertain.

nodes.text: Two records can share one mistake. Two people can borrow one story. But the dates stop moving when I do this.

choices.text: Facts are enough.
Facts need not be the whole person.

nodes.text: Then I can let the reconstruction be an act I performed, not a door I discovered.

choices.text: And what did the act change?

nodes.text: They say you gave the heirloom back. I want to believe that. Wanting is now part of the citation.
I can write 'uncertain' without writing 'meaningless.' That is the first honest label in the box.
The allotment cleared. The visits were signed. The charges were filed or they were not. Enough for history, perhaps. Not enough for hunger.
It put their photograph on my side of the table.

lines.text: They say you gave the heirloom back. I want to believe that.
The initials were gone when police found the bracelet. I had made your hand hold the file.
The money arrived every Friday before you could be brave or weak with it.
Marcus said you missed the roof and took the second bus sober. He sounded proud and annoyed.
The shelter log says you missed curfew. My version gave the night better music than the log did.
You walked toward the officer with your hands visible. Or Sam said you learned to do that later.
The freight camera caught somebody running. I chose your coat because the story already needed it.
You kept the blue crayon. I remember giving it to someone. I do not remember deciding it was you.
You entered the number in the clean little box and went anyway.
You stayed for the hearing and lost the promotion. The order does not mention that.
Someone was paid for the report. I made you choose because no tape would.
Mara remembered the returned wallet. She also remembered the pie being fresh. One of those is wrong.
You came home with a voucher and no formation. I remember the station, or a photograph of the station.
You signed again. Steady money can look like courage from far away.
You told the judge you might have chosen wrong for a real reason. That sentence exists in your voice.

scenes.stage: The laptop shows the two-bedroom apartment reconstructed from inspection photographs: second toothbrush, library books, blue crayon in a kitchen drawer.
scenes.narration: You did come back. Not all at once. There were weekends I watched the window and weekends you were already downstairs.

scenes.stage: Adult {{childName}} opens an album not included in the evidence box. Later photographs fill its pages: school pickup, a burned birthday cake, Sam asleep in a folding chair, the parent older and looking directly at the camera.
scenes.narration: I built the missing years because the years after them were ordinary enough to hide the cost. I wanted to know who climbed into our life before I was old enough to watch.

scenes.stage: Sam turns the creased photograph over. Adult {{childName}} places beside it a second print from the same afternoon. In this one the child's small hand reaches toward the camera and the parent is a blurred shape reflected in a window.
scenes.dialogue: SAM: There. Evidence from your side.

scenes.stage: The two photographs overlap. The crease completes a line from one hand to the other.
scenes.narration: I forgive the years you missed. I do not make them disappear. I keep the difference.

scenes.stage: Title card: FORGIVENESS. New Game+ unlocks. All tapes are visible from dawn.
A finance statement continues after the casualty date. The allotment reaches the guardian account on Friday, then the survivor benefit replaces it.
scenes.narration: The money came home on time. You did not.

scenes.stage: A younger Sam, seen now as interview footage rather than reconstruction, carries a folded flag to a Northside kitchen. Child {{childName}} is too short for the table and holds one corner because an adult asks them to.
scenes.narration: They taught me to call the triangle honor. It was also cloth, weight, and a reason nobody answered ordinary questions.

scenes.stage: Petty or Dominguez sits beside Sam and tells the supply-crate story before telling the ambush story. The survivor corrects one joke and cannot finish the correction.
scenes.narration: Sam gave me your dry humor. Your squad gave me the silence after it.

scenes.stage: At Fort Halvern, adult {{childName}} finds the parent's name etched among others. Their finger stops one line below it, then returns.
scenes.dialogue: ADULT CHILD: I can honor what you did without calling the risk a debt you owed me.

scenes.stage: The service ribbon rests in its empty pawn envelope beneath the name.
scenes.narration: You were not the folded flag. You were the Friday transfer, the three ruined postcards, the choice at the disabled truck, and everything the stone cannot hold.

scenes.stage: Title card: HONOR. New Game+ unlocks. All tapes are visible from dawn.

endings.name: THE CYCLE
endings.condition: custody lost and villain drift high but high-crime threshold not reached

scenes.stage: Adult {{childName}} closes the case file but leaves Marcus's voicemail on the table. A phone lights beside it with three missed calls from a contact labeled HOME.
scenes.narration: I said I was studying you. Sam said repetition can wear a lab coat.

scenes.stage: In the dark laptop screen, the adult child's face occupies the same place the parent sprite stood under Route 9. An unopened bottle sits near the sink. No music plays.
scenes.dialogue: SAM: What happens next is not evidence yet.

scenes.stage: The player receives control as the adult child. Two actions remain: CALL HOME and GO OUT. Neither displays odds, morality, or reward.

choice.result: The phone rings. Someone answers with your name, awake and unsurprised. Cut before either person speaks again.

choice.text: Take the coat and go out.
choice.result: At the door, your hand touches the photograph in the coat pocket. The door opens. Cut before the threshold.

scenes.stage: Title card: THE CYCLE. New Game+ unlocks. All tapes are visible from dawn.
The final police archive finishes loading. Dates align with the pawn ledger, the warehouse camera, and three anonymous reports. There is no remaining contradiction large enough to live inside.
scenes.narration: I had called uncertainty mercy. Then the records agreed.

scenes.stage: Sam reaches toward tape 23. Adult {{childName}} moves the box away without anger.
scenes.dialogue: ADULT CHILD: You can keep the story where they were kind to you. I am done asking it to become mine.

scenes.stage: The creased photograph goes into an archival sleeve, labeled with date, place, and photographer unknown. It is placed in the box rather than carried.
scenes.narration: A fact can be enough to stop. Stopping can be the only inheritance you accept.

scenes.stage: The box closes. No phone rings. Sam remains until the kitchen light is turned off, then leaves the key on the table.
Title card: THE FILE CLOSED. New Game+ unlocks. All tapes are visible from dawn.
